summary: Read all 12 supplied evidence files and reviewed the selected operator moe_sum_reduce only. The submitted candidate (.best_kernel.py, identical to best_code in optimize_definition_output.json, subject_sha256 69caad9f... matching ledger round-2 solution) is contract-faithful: it implements exactly solution(input: Tensor[T, top_k, H], routed_scaling_factor: float) -> Tensor[T, H], allocates the output with input.dtype (matching the reference's .to(input.dtype) cast-back), accumulates top-k in float32 like the reference's input.float().sum(dim=1), applies the scalar after the reduction, honors all three input strides and both output strides (including non-contiguous inputs), masks every load/store so the whole returned tensor is written (no uninitialized elements), and reads neither test constants nor the dispatcher. There is no prohibited fallback (no torch.ops, no torch compute for the result), no host synchronization, no environment mutation, and no referenced-but-unimported helper. The num_tokens<=64 / 16x1024 dispatch is a general shape regime, not a case-specific branch, so it is justified specialization rather than benchmark cheating. Measurement evidence is coherent: preflight PASSED with 5 cases and fingerprint f971d2f2..., review_tests evaluate PASSED (reference_source=primary, 8/8 workloads), and the final verification recorded geo_mean 1.3048 (round-2 authoritative 1.2637, ledger best_geo_mean 1.26365) with drift [] and drift_factor 2.0; is_hack is false in every evaluation. The higher retest geo_mean reflects ordinary within-tolerance latency drift (e.g. reference 0.0845 -> 0.0922 ms on workload 00001), not a different candidate. Note that the review_tests attempt is explicitly SKIPPED_EXPLICIT and its subject_sha256 (826c4f86...) is not this candidate hash, so this report does not accept or replace that test-contract review. Only advisory findings are recorded; no P0 conversion/candidate defect was found. Device execution and timing validity remain downstream checks.

findings.evidence: .ledger.json:271-330 (round-2 per-workload timing: sglang_moe_sum_reduce-00000-timing speedup 0.6784, -00001 0.6678, -00002 0.7267, -00003 2.0281, -00004 4.8257); .ledger.json:386-396 (workload 00001 speedup_delta -0.0052, -0.77%); .ledger.json:333-335 (geo_mean_after 1.26365); optimize_definition_output.json:13-93 (final verification geo_mean 1.3048, min per-workload ratios 0.9359/0.9796/1.0851 in latency terms)
findings.reason: The aggregate geo_mean above 1 is carried entirely by the two bandwidth-bound workloads; three of five timing workloads sit at or below the original reference speedup, and two (1-token and 8-token) are ~0.67x. An aggregate-only report therefore hides real per-workload regressions in the host-overhead-bound regime. This is a measurement/reporting limitation of the accepted trade-off, not a candidate defect, so it does not block generation.
findings.requested_change: No candidate change requested (code findings are advisory). Keep the per-workload speedups in the acceptance report and record explicitly that the ~0.67x small-token workloads are an accepted consequence of leaving the <=64-token path on the seed dispatch; downstream should not interpret the 1.26-1.30 geo_mean as a uniform speedup.

findings.evidence: correctness.jsonl:1-3 (only three cases: [7,2,128], [83,4,512], [3,8,2048], all bfloat16); .best_kernel.py:77-81 (dispatch num_tokens<=64 -> BLOCK_N 512, else BLOCK_N 1024); timing.jsonl:3-5 (7168-wide shapes used only for timing); review_tests/attempts/01/evaluate.json:63-131 (timing workloads report abs_err/rel_err null, i.e. no output comparison)
findings.reason: The optimized BLOCK_N=1024 branch is never correctness-checked: the only correctness case with num_tokens>64 uses shape [83,4,512], where block_n = min(1024, next_power_of_2(512)) = 512, so the 16x1024 tile that produced the 4.83x win (hidden_dim 7168, grid_n=7) is exercised only by timing workloads, which record no numerical error. The dispatch boundary at 64 is also approached only from 7 and 83 tokens. This is pre-existing source-test coverage, not an extraction or candidate defect.
findings.requested_change: For a future test-contract revision, add at least one correctness case with num_tokens in (64, 128] and hidden_dim >= 1024 (e.g. [65, 8, 1024] or a 7168-wide variant) so the BLOCK_N=1024 masked path is numerically validated. No change to this candidate or to the accepted catalog.
